parts.name: shell dome

physics.Basic_description: Large white spherical outer shell with a smooth, matte finish, forming the main protective structure of the helmet.
physics.Functional_description: Primary impact protection layer enclosing the head cavity.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasp the large curved surface with parallel jaws, ensuring wide contact to distribute force on the rigid shell.
physics.reason: Helmet shells are thin-walled composite structures enclosing air and foam padding, not solid blocks.

parts.description: Large white spherical outer shell with a smooth, matte finish, forming the main protective structure of the helmet.
parts.function: Primary impact protection layer enclosing the head cavity.

parts.name: chin trim

physics.Basic_description: Black textured rubber strip running along the lower edge and chin area of the helmet shell.
physics.Functional_description: Provides edge protection, sealing, and comfort against the neck and chin.
physics.Grasped_description: Too flexible and peripheral for a stable primary grasp; would deform under gripper pressure.
physics.reason: Rubber trim is a dense, solid extrusion or molding without significant internal voids relative to its size.

parts.description: Black textured rubber strip running along the lower edge and chin area of the helmet shell.
parts.function: Provides edge protection, sealing, and comfort against the neck and chin.

parts.name: vent 0

physics.Basic_description: Small black plastic components embedded in the shell surface, appearing as intake or exhaust vents.
physics.Functional_description: Allow airflow into and out of the helmet interior for cooling.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and flush with the surface to be grasped effectively; risk of breaking if pulled.
physics.reason: Small injection-molded plastic parts are effectively solid or have negligible hollow volume for mass estimation.

parts.name: pivot stud left

physics.Basic_description: Small cylindrical metallic stud protruding from the side of the helmet near the visor mechanism.
physics.Functional_description: Acts as a mounting point or axle for the visor pivot arm.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small to grasp reliably; would slip or damage the mechanism.
physics.reason: Metal fasteners and studs are machined solid components.

parts.description: Small cylindrical metallic stud protruding from the side of the helmet near the visor mechanism.

parts.name: pivot stud right

physics.Basic_description: Small cylindrical metallic stud on the opposite side, mirroring the left pivot.
physics.Functional_description: Mounting point for the right side of the visor mechanism.
physics.Grasped_description: Not graspable due to small size.
physics.reason: Metal fasteners are solid.

parts.description: Small cylindrical metallic stud on the opposite side, mirroring the left pivot.

parts.name: visor panel

physics.Basic_description: Large, curved, dark-tinted transparent shield covering the face opening.
physics.Functional_description: Protects the eyes and face from wind, debris, and impact while maintaining visibility.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasp the lower edge or side firmly but carefully to avoid scratching the optical surface.
physics.reason: Visors are thin sheets of polycarbonate curved into shape, enclosing air behind them.

parts.description: Large, curved, dark-tinted transparent shield covering the face opening.
parts.function: Protects the eyes and face from wind, debris, and impact while maintaining visibility.

parts.name: visor trim

physics.Basic_description: Thin black rubber strip edging the top or sides of the visor panel.
physics.Functional_description: Seals the gap between visor and shell to reduce noise and wind buffeting.
physics.Grasped_description: Flexible and thin, not suitable for load-bearing grasps.
physics.reason: Rubber seals are solid extrusions.

parts.description: Thin black rubber strip edging the top or sides of the visor panel.
parts.function: Seals the gap between visor and shell to reduce noise and wind buffeting.

parts.name: visor pivot arms

physics.Basic_description: Grey/black structural arms connecting the visor to the helmet shell pivots.
physics.Functional_description: Allows the visor to rotate up and down while maintaining alignment.
physics.Grasped_description: Can be grasped to manipulate the visor position, though care is needed to avoid stressing the pivot.
physics.reason: Structural arms are typically thick enough to be modeled as solid or ribbed solid plastic for mass purposes.

parts.description: Grey/black structural arms connecting the visor to the helmet shell pivots.
parts.function: Allows the visor to rotate up and down while maintaining alignment.

parts.name: visor axle

physics.Basic_description: Internal metallic rod or pin running through the pivot mechanism.
physics.Functional_description: Provides the rotational axis for the visor movement.
physics.Grasped_description: Internal component, not accessible for grasping.
physics.reason: Axles are solid metal rods.

parts.description: Internal metallic rod or pin running through the pivot mechanism.
parts.function: Provides the rotational axis for the visor movement.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)
simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained
